items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: who was Cannonball listening to? Willie Smith, Benny Carter, Johnny Hodges

ctx.x: Because Lord knows they’ve dissected, you know, almost every other kind of jazz.

That’s right, I know. It’s almost as if it’s an accepted corollary that if it’s happy stuff then it can’t be that serious. It’s not serious. And again, as far as I’m concerned if Louis Armstrong did it that’s serious enough for me. If Duke Ellington did it, that’s serious enough for me. If Red Allen did it, that’s serious — Jack Teagarden, and the list just goes on and on and on. And those guys, those were the guys that defined everything that we’re doing today. Those were the guys who John Coltrane and…
I thought of that yesterday when I had this recording of him doing “Stars Fell on Alabama” [scats] just like Johnny Hodges.
